utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are no preliminaries, therefore the witness can be escorted into the courtroom. I use the opportunity to deal with the following matter. On the 12th of May, the Chamber asked the Defence to file a submission on when its expert reports will be filed. The Chamber notes that 24 of the witnesses on the Defence's witness list are indicated as Rule 94 bis witnesses. On the 3rd of June, the Defence provided the Chamber and the Prosecution with an update through an informal communication. The Defence explained that four of the expert reports will be completed and filed by September 2014. These are two ballistic reports, one military report, and one demographic report. The Defence further stated that it is not in a position to predict the completion date for the report by Dr. Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Finally, the Defence indicated that it is waiting for the Registry to appoint the history, radio communications, and demolitions experts. The Chamber would be like to be kept regularly updated on the progress of the expert reports, and therefore the Defence is hereby instructed to file short updates once a month, the first one on the 20th of June of this year. Good morning, Mr. Cvoro. Again, apologies that we were still busy with other matters when you entered the courtroom. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you again --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you again that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Lukic will now continue his re-examination. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Cvoro.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need in e-court P6562.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This morning I'll go through some of the documents that were shown to you yesterday by the Prosecution, and please try to give us answers as brief as possible so we can go through it today. As we see, this is a document from the Executive Board of Pale municipality.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor questioned you on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 3 in English and page 2 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution was the most interested in this amount of 100.000 dinars for the SDS. You started to explain yesterday that funds were returned from the city but you were interrupted and you couldn't finish the explanation. What did you mean to say?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we were one of the municipalities in the city. All the contributions, all the taxes, all the fees that were collected in the city of Pale were distributed across the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was that the same situation at this time or did something change?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning with the month of January, there was some obstruction on the part of the city in the distribution, in the allocation of funds, so we couldn't properly implement our municipal budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which party had control of the city, which party was making problems?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe at the level of the city the Party of Democratic Action had majority power.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to see P6564 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the question and answer, Mr. Lukic. You said which party was making the most problems. And then the answer is that the SDA had majority power.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: SDA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did it cause problems because of its majority power?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've heard the question posed by His Honour Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the party that controls the government dictates certain things, and in this case it concerned the budget. I don't know if it was just the SDA or the coalition of parties at the level of the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I then understand that it is the SDA party which voted that an amount of 100.000 dinars should be given to the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is something special. This is the temporary financing of the municipal budget for the month of May, and the reason was that we didn't have enough funds --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. Could you please try to answer my question. You say the SDA coalition parties were controlling the budget. This is a budget, whether temporary or not. I'm asking you: Is it the decision of the SDA that this 100.000 dinars be given to the SDS, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I don't understand your question. Thank you. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that in the beginning of the year the flow of cash and payments in the city of Sarajevo was disrupted?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the city of Sarajevo, but I know there were problems in the financing of the municipalities in Pale which were part of the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then still, there is a suggestion in this answer that the -- those in power in the city of Sarajevo would have caused all this. Could you tell us in detail what caused the problems in the financing of the municipalities? Because then we know facts rather than that we are hearing suggestions in answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not participate in politics, but I was part of the executive authority and I know that we did not receive sufficient funds from the city budget.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tell us then what exactly caused this to happen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably obstruction by politicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So if I understand you well, you do not know what caused it to happen, you have some vague --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. All I know is we didn't receive the funds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your answers went further. Your answers were that they made -- the SDA made the problems because they were in power, but I do understand that you have no detailed knowledge on what exactly happened which caused you to receive less funds from the city. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did the inadequate return of funds from the city to the municipality of Pale constitute the reason why this temporary fund was created?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I then ask you one more thing. Was the SDA or were other parties not affected by the lack of adequate return of funds? What was it that specifically the SDS was suffering under it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the SDS was the only party that was active at the time. The SDA had withdrawn. It did not operate any longer. I don't know why. I don't know why they received any funds themselves. My assumption is that they were not active at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's still unclear to me, but I leave it to you, Mr. Lukic, whether you want to further explore that, why and how activity is established, activity of political organs which would then justify to pay or not to pay them, also in terms of are they still elected members of the Assembly, the municipal Assembly. I leave it to you whether you want to spend time on that, but to say they were not active therefore no money was given to them; SDS was active, and therefore they did receive money -- it would even require the basis for establishing exactly why the SDS got money, for what exactly, and whether they reported on the way in which they spent that money to those who were providing that money and that is - if I understand well - the local government. But I leave it in your hands whether you want to explore it or not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you allocate funds on request or did somebody decide independently of requests, were the SDA and the SDS supposed to apply for this money or not?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Monies were allocated strictly by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the SDS did not request funds?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they had requested them, they would have probably received them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you inquire also what law exactly applied on the funding of political parties. Perhaps the witness could answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've heard the question of Judge Orie. Can you answer?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still believe it was based on the statute of the city or the statute of municipalities. The city planned annual budget according to its statutes and within those funds financing was also envisaged for political parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I stop you there. What I asked you is whether you could tell me what statute or whatever the legal basis was exactly so that we can have a look at it, because you now say, "I still believe it was based ..." Well, I'd rather look at facts, documents, rather than what you believe the case was. Can you tell us what statute or what law it was that you applied in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know the exact law, but I know that there was Article 86 of the municipal statute as referred to in this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if Article 86 would be at one time be available so that we could have a look at it, that would be appreciated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll move on from finances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need P6564 on our screens now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, I'll give you a short introduction. You've told us that you requested fuel for the transport of refugees. This document is dated 24 May 1992. You told us there were five to ten buses filled with refugees going to Serbia every day. Were they Serb or Muslim refugees?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3038 is the next document we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These are instructions on the organising and operation of the organs of Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina in emergency conditions. This document was issued by the Serbian Democratic Party. You told us you were not a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 12 December 1991 -- 19 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 3 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that after the bullet points in both versions in the middle of the page, we read that the Crisis Staff would be headed by a commander. Did you use this title? Were you the commander of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I was the president of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know, did there exist Crisis Staffs of the SDS and Crisis Staffs of municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the Crisis Staffs of municipalities, not about Crisis Staffs of parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P6565 is the next document I would like to call up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you remember when you see it on the screen, it's a document to which the Defence objected because of certain shortcomings in the document. So I'd like to ask you: Did you ever encounter in your work documents of the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any case, you can see that this number does not have -- this document does not have a registration number?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first sentence reads: "Please find attached information ..." Can we see to whom this is addressed?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In fact, it says "to" below?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But at the end of the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the last page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the end we see there is no signature, no stamp, so we don't see who created this document. But since you never worked with SDB documents, I'll move to another type of document that is certainly more familiar to you. We will begin with P6566. Did you have any contact with Territorial Defence documents?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only had contact with the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence until the Army of Republika Srpska was established, and that was on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well, but this is a document of the Territorial Defence -- in fact, their staff.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it is the city staff or the municipal staff or the zone staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It should be the republic staff. In the documents you've seen, many of them lack registration number, this one too?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see that the documents of the TO of Pale did not have a registration number?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Law on State Administration, the rule was that all documents must be registered in the protocol.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you worked for the state administration for years [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just not to be leading, I asked: And you worked for the state administration? And the witness answered: Yes, for years. [Interpretation] Could we see page 5 in both versions. Page 3 in B/C/S, one before this. [In English] Can we move one page before this in B/C/S, please. One more. I don't know how it happened. This document has three pages. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the end of the document. We see there's no signature and no stamp?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that normal for a document of the state administration?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's compare now the first and the fourth page in B/C/S, because there are two versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll need page 1 of this document on the left side of the screen and page 4 on the right-hand side of the screen, both in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's possible to have this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying -- also inquire. Is it possible to have it? Yeah. Thank you. Now we know that it's even possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the handwritten version of the document on the left-hand side. On the left -- in the handwritten document, in the handwritten document we see that it was sent to the chief of security and then it was crossed out?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, in that version of the document, there's no such thing?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the typewritten text, we read that it was the Territorial Defence staff of the National Defence Ministry of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the handwritten version, that text is missing?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see - and I haven't finished reading - no, no, there's no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side we see "official note" at the top?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side there is no such indication?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've seen the beginning and the end of this document. Can we see who created it without the signature, without the typewritten name, without a stamp?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We can't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One clarification, you said, Mr. Lukic: "On the right-hand side we see 'official note' at the top." I take it you mean right-hand side of the screen but left-hand side of the handwritten document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked something about P2001. It hasn't even been shown to you so there's no need for me to show it either. It was marked. Mandic, 22153 is our transcript page. I'm going to read out the question that was put to you. It's line 15. It had to do with Mandic and Stanisic. [In English] I quote --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read it out to you now and you're going to receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] "Now, my first focused question for you, Mr. Mandic and Mr. Stanisic were both officials in the Bosnian Serb Ministry of the Interior; correct?" And your answer was in line 18: "Yes, that's correct. They were in the leadership."

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I'm putting to you: That Mandic was not a member of the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly he wasn't. I know that he was part of the leadership; maybe he wasn't within the MUP structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now I would like to know what the witness knows about Mandic, what was his duty? What was his position? What was his rank? Where was he situated? At which time? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not sure. Now that Mr. Lukic put this question to me -- I think he was in the Ministry of Justice, not in the Ministry of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What was his position and his duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I'm saying that once again, but he may have been the minister, actually, because ministers changed. I don't know who it was at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the clarity of the record, I think it might be useful for Mr. Lukic to specify what time-period he's talking about. Many officials held different jobs at different times during the indictment period, Mr. Mandic included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, I wonder whether the parties could not agree on who was in what ministry at what point in time. I mean, these were not secret appointments; these were public functions. So, Mr. Traldi, if you would like to know whether Mr. Mandic was in what position at the moment that this happened, why not seek an agreement with Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll speak at the break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's better than to ask a witness who says he's not certain about it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Now we need P3972, that's the document we'd like to have displayed on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We know -- actually, we discussed this document yesterday. It is document -- it is a document of the Municipal Assembly of Pale. The Prosecutor showed you page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would kindly ask for page 4 in both versions as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Judges asked yesterday also what had been done because you explained that previously there had been attempts to move people out, there was this lack of understanding, you explained to people that they didn't have to leave. We see here in paragraph 2 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English actually we'd have to go down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you referring to item 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, item 2, point 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 2 here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is written here is that: "The president of the Assembly and the president of the Executive Board" -- so you're the latter; right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it says: "... objected to the activities of the public security station in this respect because it had taken part in attempts to move the Muslims out, which was done without a political decision which meant that the official structures of power had been bypassed." And then it says, I quote: "This is why the attempt had been stopped." So what was stopped, these attempts to --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exercise or exert pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the English version we have the right paragraph now. Now the next paragraph, this is what I'm going to read out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Lukic. Could you tell us exactly then what you did to prevent that because I think earlier you said you had no authority over others. What did you then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, our commissioner was Mrs. Biljana Plavsic for our municipality. We intervened through her, and she, in accordance with her authority, intervened to have these occurrences prevented, or rather, stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It makes a difference whether it was prevented or whether it was stopped, the difference being that if it is prevented that the attempts never materialised. If you stop it, then it has happened but then you discontinued that to happen. Now, what was it, was it prevented or was it stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stopped, as we've stated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, the translation says it was prevented, but let's -- and then could you tell us exactly in what way, then, did you seek the intervention of Madam Plavsic in writing or did you -- how did this happen, this stopping this event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, every day we had meetings with Mrs. Biljana Plavsic -- well, I cannot say every day, almost every day, and we informed her about the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what did she then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She gave us certain instructions as to how we should act, the executive, that is, and also she provided instructions how other organs should act, those that are not within the executive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did she say how you would have to act?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, what was stated was that we should do everything to stop that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What then is the -- what did you then do to stop it? I mean -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we went out into the field, we went to the actual places involved, and this is one aspect of our activity and our work, as far as the executive is concerned. Again, I'm speaking about the executive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was done by the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the police probably knows how and in which way they acted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The "probably" suggests that you do not know precisely; is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we were not satisfied with their work and that is why we informed the Assembly of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you then inform the Assembly after you had sought the intervention of Madam Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, after, I mean -- actually, first we informed Mrs. Plavsic and then we convened the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Yes, now I'm re-reading your answers. I asked you: "Could you tell us exactly what you did to stop it or prevent it?" And you said: "Well, our commissioner was Mrs. Biljana Plavsic for our municipality. We intervened through her and she intervened to have these occurrences prevented, or rather, stopped." But I do understand that as far as you are concerned, what she did is tell you to do whatever was needed to stop it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that we had to stop that and that we had to go out into the field and speak to the Muslims so that, I mean -- well, that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You spoke to the Muslims or you spoke to those who were attempting to drive them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we talked to the Muslims. And those who made these attempts, well, that was within the scope of work of the police because it is for the police to establish the reasons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do you know exactly what then the police did in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what happened is you went to Biljana Plavsic, that she told you to do everything to stop it, that you then just talked to the Muslims, and that you do not know what the police did in addressing those who attempted to expel the Muslims; is that a summary of what you told us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although you don't know exactly what the police did specifically, concretely, the situation, or rather, the attempts to have people move out by force, that was stopped all together; right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written in this Assembly material under number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it also your recollection that it stopped completely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, that is my recollection. The police started this action to replace the commander and the chief, and I know there were some problems probably in respect of these questions but I'm not aware of any details and I cannot really talk about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was for this reason, was the commander and the chief replaced because the police had expelled them? I'm just trying to understand your answer. Mr. Lukic, your microphone is still open so I do not know what ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether he was replaced then, but I know that there was this activity concerning the replacement of the chief and the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I asked you because you raised it in the context of the question that was put to you about what exactly the police had done. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have much time left so we'll have to -- well, actually, I'm going to skip a few things --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the time the Chamber uses for asking questions is carefully administered so it does not go from your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm trying to finish in the first session so we have enough time for the next witness, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next paragraph in this document, this is what it says, I quote: "In order to keep the discussion focused, the Assembly proposed that a Working Group formulate a draft decision on the moving out of Muslims and Croats, stressing in it that the departure of these people from the territory of the municipality should be done on a voluntary basis and in an organised manner."

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this decision, was the principle of voluntariness and departure in an organised manner emphasised?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need P264.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a brief document issued by the public security station of Pale on the 2nd of July, 1992, and there is this section where it says "decision." And it said that the request made by citizens of Muslim and Croat ethnicity is being granted, that they can move out of the municipality of Pale, unobstructed, as they wish.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had it not been for these requests, would you have taken part in moving out citizens from Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you believe that you did not have the right to stop these people from leaving?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. We wouldn't have the right to do that. I mean, had they not submitted this request, that would have been different, but since they had submitted this request, then it is their civic right to decide where they want to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, in the last paragraph, we can see that police and military patrols are to enable the unobstructed passage of buses.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These buses, at the time were they supposed to pass through check-points, were they already there?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, practically they were supposed to pass through the separation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's my next question.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the territory there weren't any check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. So were they supposed to cross the front line?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, would they have succeeded in crossing this front line safely without this escort?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need document P3800.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document was shown to you yesterday as well. Again, this is a report of the public security station of Pale dated the 6th of July, 1992, and this provides an idea as to who left the municipality of Pale.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, it says that it was done at the requests made by these citizens and that this was enabled by the municipality of Pale.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this a public process? Was it open to the public?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And as for the document itself, on the document itself we see that it hasn't been marked as a state secret; right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It hasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said to us that these people who decided to move out left, some took buses, others took passenger vehicles along with their personal belongings?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that for sure, that some left on buses and others took their own motor vehicles and all the personal belongings that they could take along.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, the end of June, the beginning of July, 1992, could Serbs leave Sarajevo with their cars and their movable property?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd just like -- I'd just tentatively object and ask that some foundation be laid for the witness's knowledge in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm, that's my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then please put that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, were people coming to Pale from Sarajevo, or up until then, had refugees already arrived from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many refugees came through a local road. That is to say, all communications with Sarajevo had been cut off, and they took military vehicles and other means of transportation as they managed. They could not take their own motor vehicles. They did not come in an organised fashion. They didn't come on buses either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, you're telling us about people who managed to escape?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That is why we had a large number of refugees in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more document and then we'll be done, at least I will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is P6574.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I put one or two questions to the witness in this context. Why could the Serbs from Sarajevo not use their own vehicles to reach Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all roads that went from Sarajevo to Pale were under control. On the one hand, I mean Muslim forces; and on the other hand, Serb forces. These roads had been closed down. Then what was being built was, well, across hills. I mean, roads were being built with certain machines in order for people to be able to get to Pale and that's how they got there. Buses could not take these roads, not even vehicles could take those roads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, how could the Muslims from Pale then move to Sarajevo with their own cars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was organised, a convoy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have similar documentation about convoys, because we see on our screen -- we saw on our screen how buses were organised and escorted, et cetera. Apparently there were written instructions for that. Do you have -- do there exist similar written instructions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for convoys of vehicles -- vehicles owned by Muslims who wanted to leave with their own cars? Do similar documents exist, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, unfortunately documents only say that they took buses, but I know that they would also leave in passenger motor vehicles too but I don't have any documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means all those in buses, did they leave any motor cars privately owned behind in Pale, or were these just people who were not in the possession of personal motor cars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, mostly those who did not have motor vehicles were on buses, whereas those who had motor vehicles joined the buses and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, my question was whether those on the buses left behind any motor cars as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen we see a document and you protested when the Prosecutor asked you about this because it concerns 1995. But I'm just going to ask you to read out the introductory paragraph. The question is whether Renovica was in Serb hands or in Muslim hands. When you read the beginning of the document, do you come to the conclusion that at that time Renovica was in Serb hands or in Muslim hands at that time, the end of 1995 or just before that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to what we learned from the captured Muslim fighters, they will be pulled out along three different axes and so on; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now point 2 --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point 2, well, it says, Dzimrije, Sokolovici, Stjenice, Renovica, and so on, the left bank of the river Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go on to number 3 -- no, below number 3.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All directions are mainly unpopulated and before the war they were populated by Muslim inhabitants for the most part. The most probable directions of their movement and disengagements are directions one and three because they are closest to Gorazde ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can you draw a conclusion? If not --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that Renovica was -- parts of it around the barracks were under the control of the Serb forces for a while, but when the barracks withdrew, Renovica and parts of Praca were captured by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvoro. This is all I had for you. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I ask you if you have any questions, Judge Moloto would have one question -- one or more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question I'm going to ask you, you might have been asked by Judge Orie but I'm not quite sure I understood the answer. You've told us that Muslims left in buses and private cars from Pale to Sarajevo; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You also told us, and I quote page 23, lines 7 to 10, you say: "Many refugees came through a local road." And these are Serb refugees from Sarajevo. "That is to say, all communications with Sarajevo had been cut off, and they took military vehicles and other means of transportation as they managed. They could not take their own motor vehicles, they did not come in an organised fashion. They didn't come on buses either." My question is: If communications had been cut and refugees from Sarajevo could not come in their cars, had to use military trucks, what roads were used by the Muslims who went to Sarajevo and why is it they were able to go in private cars and buses?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the order from the commander or the chief of the public security station discusses that precisely, what roads and what communications and in what way they left for Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, let me stop you. I understand -- the order might discuss that. I'm asking you what roads were used by the Muslim refugees to go to Sarajevo which could not be used by the Serb refugees from Sarajevo to Pale, irrespective of what is discussed in the order. I'm asking you for the roads.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. Well, that's the road going from Pale to -- via Hresa, Vasin Han, and of course then through the Muslim parts, Travnik and so on and so forth. That is the normal road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And why could Serbs not use the same road?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because they weren't allowed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Allowed by who?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, I'm asking for facts, not probabilities.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because the roads were closed. There was no passing through them. The roads were mined, there were barricades, there were separation lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if the roads were mined, how did the Muslims go through them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably they removed certain -- well, I'm talking about our side and our road. In agreement with the Muslim forces that road was cleared, it was freed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I had one area, but Mr. Lukic and I agreed that one document would be admitted. I can inform the Chamber the number and it will spare us from any further questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then, Mr. Cvoro, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for having answered the many, many questions, not only by the parties but also by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The document which would be admitted, Mr. President, is 65 ter 30715. It must be admitted under seal due to protective measures in a different case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We may have a look at it. It cannot be -- well, if it is shown on our screens, then it's not to be published --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but before we decide on admission, we usually would like to know what we are admitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to have it shown as long as it's not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I can provide more detail on the relevance, in my view, Your Honours, but I'd request to do it in private session if that would assist the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps it's better to do it now than -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think this is something you asked for yesterday, so I think that Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You don't object, we asked for it, then it's clear. Then there was one translation issue left over of yesterday. It had got something to do with the forceful or -- you remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any further report on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I can inform the Chamber that we've contacted CLSS. A new translation has been uploaded under the doc ID Y015-0027-1-ET. We received it this morning and at whatever leisure the Defence is able to review it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no objection against --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not yet, unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We just received it during the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one line -- the one line is -- are you able to read that one line which caused the whole thing so that the Chamber ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The translation I have -- well, perhaps we could call it up by doc ID. Has it been released?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for the record, this is P6572 that's at issue. That's the document that should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps we first take the break and then -- but there's one thing, Madam Registrar, 65 ter number 30715 has not been assigned a number yet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30715 receives number P6575, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal. Then we take a break and we will resume at 11.00. And during the break, the necessary measures will be taken -- the protective measures will be installed. We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the next witness to be escorted into the courtroom, we need to go into closed session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness GRM311, because that's how we will call you, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please be seated. Witness, you will testify and we'll not use your own name, you'll testify under pseudonym, your pseudonym being Witness GRM311. No one will see your face outside this courtroom. No one will hear your own voice. Please keep in mind that if any question touches upon a matter which might reveal your identity, that you then ask for private session, and the parties are also -- are also reminded that they should take care to ask for private session whenever that would be needed in order to make the protective measures effective. Witness, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic -- no, by Mr. Ivetic, although Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have a few words before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the break, Mr. Traldi offered one document, actually corrected translation, under number ID Y015-0027-1-ET. We checked the translation during the break and we do not object to this translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's all I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'd request to replace it -- request leave to replace it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, leave is granted to replace the original English translation by the newly uploaded one. And that was in relation to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: P6572, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6572. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I would just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- ask for myself and Mr. Traldi to be excused, both of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's very kind of you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and, Witness, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to call up 65 ter number 1D02794, but please do not broadcast the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would draw your attention to this document, which is a pseudonym sheet, and I would ask that you confirm if your name and birth-date are set forth correctly on this document?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would move to admit 1D02794 into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2794 receives number D508, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document I would like to call up also should not be broadcast, it is 1D01619 in e-court. And I have a hard copy, with the assistance of the usher, for the witness after the Prosecution checks to see that it's a clean copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the screen we have a witness statement. Can you please confirm for us if that is your signature that appears on the bottom of the first page in the original?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to review the statement in the Serbian language during proofing subsequent to having signed the same?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 4 in the English, page 4 in the Serbian, again not broadcasting the same, and focus on paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, here in paragraph 13 where it says: "The mortars were in front of the Army Hospital in Sarajevo." Do you wish to correct that entry?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: The launchers were within the perimeter of the military hospital, not outside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Apart from this one change, do you stand by your statement and affirm that everything therein is accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you the same questions today about the topics covered in the statement, would your answers be the same in substance?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I would answer the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now that you have taken the solemn declaration, would those answers as contained in this statement be truthful?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would move for the witness statement to be admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The Prosecution does not object to the admission of this witness's statement; however, we maintain the position that we put in the response to the Defence 92 ter motion for this witness, that the majority of the evidence is tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1619 receives number D509, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. At this time I would read the public summary of the statement, the purpose of which has been explained to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The witness is an ethnic Serb who spent the war in Sarajevo on the territory controlled by the ABiH. The witness was ordered to produce hand-grenades for the ABiH at a civilian factory. The witness worked 12 hours straight at this job daily. The witness knows that Bosnian Muslim youths were going around with a list of persons to throw grenades at and that the Bosnian Muslims killed their own to increase the number of casualties. At home the witness's utilities were cut off and a neighbour told him it was because he was a Serb. Due to that, the witness had to collect firewood to take home with him. On three occasions while collecting wood, the witness found dead bodies with black bags over their heads. On 5 January 1993, while going home from work, the witness was taken by two men wearing balaclavas who put a bag over his head and drove him in a van towards Pofalici. There they showed him a massacre of more than ten bodies cut up and piled in a pit, with a decapitated child on the top of the pile, its severed arms in the shape of a cross. Next to the child's body was a woman, on whose chest the head of the child had been placed. These men beat the witness and cursed his Serbian mother, saying that if he did not continue making grenades for the Muslims, he would end up the same as the people who had been killed in the pit. The witness says the BH authorities shut down the city and kept it that way. He had to pay money to various Bosnian Muslim and Croat officials in order to get members of his family out of Sarajevo. The witness recalls that the Bosnian Muslim side positioned weapons at public institutions, like schools, health centres, and hospitals. The witness saw the ABiH firing mortars from the army hospital and a machine-gun nest near the health centre by Kumrovec. The witness was forced out of Sarajevo in 1996. A Bosnian Muslim was given his apartment to keep that man quiet because he knew that his wife had been killed by the ABiH side and not the Serb side. And that ends the summary of the statement for this witness. I would ask to go briefly into private session for some follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could please turn to page 3 in both languages of D509 under seal and focus on paragraph 7 of the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this paragraph you describe an incident in January of 1993 when you were taken away and beaten, and you mentioned 11 prior occasions. Can you please explain for us what you meant by reference to 11 prior occasions?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: On my way to work, on the way back from work, usually on the way back, people I didn't know stopped me on 11 different occasions. They took me to show me the crimes that they had committed in order, I suppose, to kill me mentally. Every time I was beaten and every time I was threatened and told that I shouldn't meet anyone, and they would ask me, as I've already said in my earlier answer, who I had met and what I was doing there and what I was looking for, which was all made up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did those individuals also make reference to your work?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object. That's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ivetic, could you phrase the question in such a way that you do not find objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the individuals who took you away appear to know who you were? Did they make any reference to your identity?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, they knew exactly who I was, where I was working, and what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you mention in your statement that you needed to make grenades. What was the requirement of you and the other two coworkers for the daily output for each of you for these grenades?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: In a 12-hour shift I needed to make 120 grenades. And if we stayed until 10.00 p.m., then we needed to make 150 grenades each.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 7 of your written statement you identify that on this occasion when these men took you out, they told you that you needed to keep -- continue making bombs for the Muslims. Is that all that they referenced in relation to your work or did these men who took you away make any additional comments about your work?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: While they were taking me away they kept asking the same questions: With whom I was collaborating, to whom I was reporting, and to whom I had reported that one of the Muslims needed to be killed, and they called me an accomplice in all these things, which wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would now like to take a look at page 4 in English and page 5 in Serbian at paragraph 16 of your statement, which goes on to the next page in the English. Sir, in this paragraph you state that you found at the Marin Dvor school Muslims killed their own people. Could you please explain what you meant by that comment?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1992, as I was leaving the workshop where I was working, I ran into three boys who carried in their school bags hand-grenades made by me. They were standing by a man who was also working in the factory who knew them, and he pointed to me and said: Here is the man who knows all about these things. So they were introduced to me. The boys were 15 or 16 years of age, and they said that in the secondary mechanical engineering school at Marin Dvor they had undergone training in what I would call sabotage. They had shells in their school bags, each could hold 12 grenades so that they wouldn't move around. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can please ask to have called up Exhibit P0003, page 20 in e-court. And again, if we can have the assistance of the usher to assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to have you mark with an X any buildings that are visible in this photograph where ABiH soldiers were situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are there any other buildings where there were ABiH soldiers situated that are visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. MacGregor --

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honours. I'm concerned that the references that the witness is making with the exhibit are potentially identifying and that we possibly should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you have occasion to know of any situation where the ABiH used heavy weapons to fire upon their own territory; and if so, could you tell us the circumstances of that?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, on the way to the factory, not far away from TV Sarajevo, where the Miljacka River flows, and then the TV building is separated from the parking-lot for trams. They call that Remiza. Every day two weapons were firing from there. Mostly these shells would detonate in Svrakino Selo and Hrasno Brdo. The following day after that, all the Sarajevo media reported that criminals from the hills destroyed Svrakino Selo and they mentioned the number of casualties, victims, and also from Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you identify for us when the Sarajevo media talked about criminals from the hills, who were they understood by you to be referencing?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: They were talking about the Serb forces that were defending their territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the territory that you identified, Svrakino Selo and Hrasno Brdo, under whose -- whose territory were those positions located within?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Those territories were under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions in direct for this witness and I thank you for the additional extension of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to inform the parties that there was a specific request which will be relayed to you from the Victims and Witness Section. Could you please consider that. It's about timing, it's nothing very special. First the witness should be escorted out of the courtroom, and for that reason we will turn into closed session. We will remain in closed session when we take a break. And when resuming at 25 minutes past 12.00, we'll start in closed session and immediately after that turn into open session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. MacGregor, if you are ready to cross-examine the witness. Witness GRM311, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. MacGregor. Ms. MacGregor, you'll find her to your right and she's counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness. I'm going --

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'm going to try to finish my exam today so that you can go home as soon as possible, and I will do that by asking specific questions. You can help me do that by listening closely to what I ask and only answering those questions that I ask. My first question is: Is it correct that you were a witness for the Defence before this Tribunal in the trial of Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. MacGregor, you should switch off your microphone when the witness is answering.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: That was in July 2007?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If we can please go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Starting in May 1992 and up until June of 1994, you worked nearly every day at the factory?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Not nearly every day, every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And during that period you would be gone from your flat from approximately 5.00 a.m. until 8.00 or 9.00 p.m.; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: After my injury, it was from 10.00 in the evening until 4.00 in the morning, in the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I may have misunderstood. I'm talking about in the period from May 1992 to June 1994 when you were working, what hours were you in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: At that time I was in the apartment from 8.00 in the evening until 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you. You've discussed two other employees at the factory besides yourself. Were there other employees manufacturing other items in the factory at that same time?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: The man who prepared bodies of the shells for processing on the machine, he was there but none of the other manufacturers. Maybe I should explain this to you a bit -- I do apologise. As for working on a machine, it was necessary to cut pipes and prepare the top and the bottom, to weld that together, and then come to the machine to process it further. This man who was involved in the manufacturing, in addition to the three of us, he was a welder and that is what he had done before coming to work with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The pipes you describe, is it like the pole that a street sign would sit on?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I don't know where they came from. It was phi 50, that is to say, the external diameter was 50 and 75 metres was the length.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And your job was to cut these long pipes into small sections of pipe?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Somebody else cut those pipes, probably the person who welded the top and the bottom. You see, I would just process the part that was given to me on the basis of a drawing and I dealt with that on the machine. Somebody else had prepared it for this processing beforehand. If you allow me, I could explain this to you so that you could understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, unfortunately we don't --

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: For example, I cut this thing here and --

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I think we have enough on the record to understand, and I'm trying to help you get home, but I do understand it's interesting.

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: It's correct that the cylinders after they were complete, they were not filled with a fuse or a charge at your factory; that happened elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, that happened at the mechanical technical school at Marin Dvor. That was about 300 metres away from the factory as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Would you describe the job you did as physically demanding?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Between 1992, at least until June 1994, you received a salary from the factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, I received some compensation, something.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And the factory also provided you with your residential flat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes. I got that flat about ten years before the war -- no, no, I'm sorry. It was three years before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Now, as the only Bosnian Serb working with only Muslims, did you have any problems at work with your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No, I did not at work, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: You were not threatened while at work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And you never threatened to quit your job; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I want to talk now about the experience you had that you describe in your statement at the pit in paragraphs 5 and 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that's Exhibit D509, I believe, that's the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Now, according to your statement -- first of all, are you familiar with which event I'm talking about involving the pit where you saw the bodies?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: According to your statement, this happened in January of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes. More specifically, on the 5th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 30763, page 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: As we wait for this to come up on the screen, Mr. Witness, it's again testimony that you made during your Milosevic case. So again, I'll have to read it to you, as it's not in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If you can focus, please, on the bottom half of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Okay. I'm reading from line number 15. This is your testimony: "I was taken away during my work there on 11 occasions. The most drastic example occurred in early November of 1992 ..." And you continue to describe the episode at the pit. Is this the same episode that you've now today said occurred in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not receive interpretation at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for this date that was mentioned here, it was -- it's not correct. Somebody must have made a mistake. The correct date is 5 January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If I can please have e-court page 51 of the same document, again towards the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, later in the same testimony, the Prosecutor again asked you about the date when you saw various atrocities. I'm going to read to you your response to that question. This is at line 18 of the screen in front of us. "... I recall that on that earlier incident when they took me to see that pit, that was on the 27th of October, 1992. I wanted to write about that, but then they searched my flat and they found some pieces of paper where they said I had noted down some of the dates, and after this happened I no longer wrote about this." Mr. Witness, did you write some notes, including the date, about the incident you saw at the pit?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Are you referring to these dates, 5 January 1992, or rather, and 1992? Is that the date you're referring to or those dates?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: My question is: Did you write down notes about the incident you saw at the pit? That's my first question.

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I noted some dates even before this, before 5 January. On the 5th of January I remember well when I was thrown out, when they threw me out of the car into a ditch and it was dark. It was a concrete ditch and I know that one of these men said: Oh, he's going to have a good Christmas. And there is no doubt about it that there was a mistake made there, that this wasn't 5 January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If I can please turn to page 53 of the document that we have up. This is again from the same testimony on this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: At line 12, the Prosecutor asks: "And the incident with the pit was in October 1992; is that right?" And your answer is: "1992."

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No, no, that's not how it was. And I affirmed this precisely because of what I've just said, how this man mentioned that on the following day or two days later, it was Christmas and that I would celebrate it well following this. So somebody else made that mistake, not me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when you testified in the Milosevic case you did not say that the pit incident happened on Serb Christmas Eve, did you?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No, I did not say that. I did not because I was sure that I said it was on the 5th of January and that it would be without this compensation that this man mentioned, that that's how it would be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to a slightly different topic. The Prosecution received from the Defence a report of information that you've given in the past few days since you've been in The Hague. In that report the information provided says that you stated that every time you were abducted, you were taken into a van which was a red van. Do you remember telling the Defence that in the past couple days?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yeah, but no, it wasn't a red van, it was black. The van was black, not red.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not asked Ms. Stewart to upload the information report into e-court because I don't intend to ask that it be put into evidence, but if possible, I'll raise that at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
