utterances.text: Yes, now first of all, does it contain reference to a red van? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It does, Your Honour, the B/C/S words are close for both. I may have -- I prepared the information report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just -- I'm just trying to seek whether the parties agree on that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree it does say "red" in the information report drafted by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- those words are written in there. Please proceed, Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that as a result of this incident at the pit, your arm and your leg were broken and you could barely stand or walk; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And after your arm and your leg were broken, you remained employed at the factory until June -- employed and working daily at the factory until June 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: You worked the same hours that you worked before the incident at the pit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: During that period, you continued to walk to and from work daily along the same route; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And you had the same tasks at the factory that we've just discussed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Now, in June 1994, approximately 18 months later, you approached a Croatian doctor about your injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, today at temporary transcript page 40, today you stated that you were abducted about 11 times. And in your statement you say, in paragraph 7, when you're describing the incident at the pit, that you had been taken away before some 11 times while returning home from work. I understand this to mean that before the pit incident you were taken 11 other times; am I understanding that correctly?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Throughout the period of my work there, I was taken away 11 times, before and after the pit, 11 times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And the last time that it happened, do you recall what the date was the last time it happened?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No. I apologise, I remember that it was on the 27th of April, 1993, and on that occasion I saw a man, I saw what he looked like. This wasn't the case before because they had masks on. Early in the morning I was on my way to work, my leg was broken, and a black -- when a black car, some kind of limousine, stopped between the Novi Grad municipality and Sarajevo TV. The man offered me a ride. I refused and then he offered again. He said: Why don't you get inside. I see you can barely walk. You are going to work, aren't you? He had a shaved head and a long beard. He asked me, obviously knowing where I worked, he asked me whether it was difficult work and I said: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, sorry --

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: At the place where I was supposed to get off at the social security administration --

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. Witness, I'm trying to keep us on pace. My question is merely to ask you -- and I'll just clarify. So April 27th, 1993, is the last time you remember an incident where you were taken away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I think there weren't any other abductions. If there were any other encounters, it would have only been they would pull me into one of the entrances and ask me: Where were you? What were you doing? And so on. But this was just harassment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If I can please have 65 ter 30763, e-court page 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Again, I'm bringing up some of your testimony from the Milosevic case. If we can look -- I'm looking at a section where the Prosecutor in that case asked you a similar question, asked you when was the last time that you were abducted. If we can focus on around line 12, I'll read it to you, sir, since you don't have it in B/C/S. Your answer was: "The last time it happened it was in August of 1994, when, again, I was placed in a black van where there were four persons who had been tied up. I was taken somewhere in the territory of Pofalici, and before my very eyes all of the four people were shot to death. They threatened me that the same thing would happen to me the following day unless I went to work." Now, this incident is not included in the statement that you've made for this case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I didn't say many things, not even on this occasion. I didn't say everything to Mr. Ivetic. I didn't say that it had already been ready, everything had already been prepared six months in advance, there were some 6.000 hand-grenades that were supposed to be retrofitted. So the factory where I was working, it had been already full of hand-grenades that were just to be processed and finished. I can't -- so this is the first time I'm saying it. I can't remember everything after all the mistreatment and everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you. The incident that I've just read about to you, that occurred after you were no longer working at the factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, on my way to the doctor's.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: So presumably you did not go to work the following day as you were threatened to do?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No, I did not go to work. From the first day when I was put on sick leave, I never worked after that. I only went to the factory when I needed to get a referral for a specialist examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Let's move actually now to that time while you were on sick leave. Your treatment that you received was from the Kosevo hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: From June 1994 until the middle of 1996, you received treatment at the Kosevo hospital every seven days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No. I went there monthly, every month, because every time when I saw the doctor she would extend my sick leave for another month.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If we can have e-court page 64, please, of the document that's currently on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that, I would have one additional question for you, Witness. You said about an incident some kind of a limousine that stopped. Through the interpretation you may not be aware that I'm putting a question to you at this moment, but I think you earlier said it was always vans. Was that only one time that it was a limousine or did it happen more often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that it was always a black van, and on this occasion it was a black limousine. The man wouldn't stop where I was supposed to get off, but took me to the Bristol Hotel, to the entrance to the Orthodox Church and he told me: Look what they're doing to us. He said he was also a Serb. There were three human heads hanging on the front door handle, severed heads. And then he said: You can pass here quickly to the factory. As I crossed to the factory, I ran into an even greater horror, pack of stray dogs, some 15 of them, tearing into each other. When I wanted to pass by, I saw that three of them had human heads hanging around their necks, and they were fighting each other to eat into them. That was on the 27 April ’93. I arrived earlier because this man had given me a lift, and the armed men at the factory gate would not let me in. They made me go farther away, I don't know what they were doing there. I returned again at five to 7 and entered the factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where exactly were those bodies? Were they in the church or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were at the door of the church, on the handle of the entrance door, three severed heads were hung on the door. It is the Church of Holy Transfiguration in Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the dogs would then bite in those heads; is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you said a minute ago: "They were biting them and biting off parts of their bodies," what did you then have on your mind if they were biting into the heads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. They were biting each other, fighting over who would get to the human head first because obviously those dogs were hungry. They were attacking those dogs who had human heads tied around their necks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure that the witness is clearly understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you -- then again, biting off parts of their bodies, as you said before, was that one dog biting off parts of the body of another dog or -- it's not entirely clear to me. Could you further explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Other dogs attacked those dogs that had the human heads hung from their necks. Other dogs attacked them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did they bite off parts of the bodies of those other dogs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see that. It's very hard to see that. I was trying to pass by as quickly as possible so they wouldn't tear into me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said the human heads hung from their necks, from the necks of the dogs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I interrupted when you -- I think the last question that was put to you was about the frequency of treatment in Kosevo hospital. I think you said it was monthly, and Ms. MacGregor was now wants to put part of previous testimony to you. That's where we were, Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just interrupt, Ms. MacGregor. This incident with the dogs, did it happen before or after the incident at the pit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: After. And you say on this day you ran into a pack of dogs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You were able to run notwithstanding the broken leg that you sustained at the pit incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This sounds a bit funny to me as a conclusion, but... forgive me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To run into and to come across are the same thing. I only moved with speed when I was thrown into that pit among the corpses. The rest of the way I walked as slowly as I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, please carefully listen to the next question of Ms. MacGregor. She -- the last thing she asked about your treatment at Kosevo hospital was whether -- what the frequency was and I think you said it was monthly because your sick leave would be extended every month. And that's where Ms. MacGregor now resumes. Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The e-court page that I need on the screen is actually e-court page 18. Ms. Stewart corrected me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'm turning to a portion of your testimony from Milosevic trial that was about your treatment at Kosevo hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And if we can please scroll down a bit towards line 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'll read to you from the transcript starting actually at line 20. "When I went on sick-leave in mid-1994, every seven days I would go to my doctors for a checkup. On my way there, I had to pass by the military hospital ..." Mr. Witness, is it your testimony today that you went to the Kosevo hospital every seven days or that you went once a month?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Yeah. And I will just ask one more question and then I know that it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Just a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Just to be clear, you walked from your flat to the Kosevo hospital approximately -- approximately every seven days between June 1994 and mid-1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us an indication as to how much time you would still need after the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: 35 minutes, 30 minutes, I'm doing my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm also looking at you, Mr. Ivetic, because 30 minutes and then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After we resume that would -- how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right now I have only one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Only one or two questions. That might, then, be resolved with an extended session of 10 to 15 minutes. I asked Madam Registrar to inquire whether that would be possible. We turn into closed session for the witness to leave the courtroom and we'll resume in closed session at ten minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. MacGregor, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: We were talking before the break about the walk you made from your flat to the Kosevo hospital. Is the distance between those two places approximately 7 to 8 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, even more.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And that walk took you about two hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And in part because of your injuries you walked slower than you normally would; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit 65 ter 30766, not to be broadcast, as it shows the location of the witness's residence. And, Your Honours, I have printed large copies of the map, if the usher can assist me to bring those up for you, it may help you as we look through this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, on the screen in front of you is a map of Sarajevo that you marked during your testimony in the Milosevic trial. Now, do you see that, sir, on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: My eyesight is not good because the criminals who had taken me away made me almost blind with the bags full of chemicals they put on my head, so I don't see well. But let's try.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'll ask, perhaps it can be zoomed in slightly to assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see there's a red line going along --

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Is that red line -- does that represent the path that you took from your flat to the Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking at audible volume.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I believe you just answered --

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes. Here, the map does not show Kosevo hospital. This map shows Marin Dvor up to the military hospital and the exit towards the institute of hygiene, but it doesn't show the Kosevo hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Kosevo hospital would be off of this map to the north-east approximately?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I don't understand this very well. I know that Kosevo hospital is not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, is there any disagreement between the parties where Kosevo hospital is in relation to this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the Chamber is -- so we could -- if the witness tells us Kosevo hospital and we know that -- at least we have seen that before on maps that it is a relatively large compound or large area where the various buildings of the Kosevo hospital are to be found. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: For your reference, Your Honours, the map in Exhibit P0003, e-court page 72, hard copy page 65, shows that complex marked as 71, and the military hospital which we will be discussing is marked as 72.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I wanted to ask you a few questions about your walk -- your route to the hospital that you took. If you can give me one moment. Okay. As you would be leaving your flat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, since we moved in, it's not visible anymore. If we move out again, we find at least the extreme parts of Kosevo hospital still on the monitor. There we are at the very right top. It's -- even an H is found there. You see it? So now we all have it even on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: The view we have on the screen will be helpful right now hopefully for the witness with the next series of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, this should be the Kosevo hospital marked with an H; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, if you can not mark the map at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness said that it was marked --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. And that is, an H appears where approximately the Kosevo hospital apparently is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Okay. If we can zoom out a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I have some questions about the route you took and you can use the map as a reference, but also you can just rely on your memory. Now, across the Bulevar Mese Selimovica, across that street from Alipasino Polje, is that where the PTT building was located?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: You may need to move the map slightly to the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember now exactly. It's still there but I can't see it because I don't see it well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move in where -- I take it that we need the left part of the -- that road, that area. Move in -- zoom in a bit more perhaps even.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, from your memory, is that where the PTT building is located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Ms. MacGregor asked you to answer the question using your memory. Is the PTT building located next to the main big road between the -- between Alipasino Polje and Marin Dvor, is it on that main road? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember. I can't. I'm not sure and I don't want to make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll move on. And actually, why don't we pull the map off the screen for the time being. I may come back to it in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Please just answer the questions based on your knowledge of the town. Okay, as you would walk from your residence to the Kosevo hospital, is it correct that you would pass the Marsal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, but from the side facing the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: To be clear, I'm asking about the route you drew on the map which is along the Bulevar Mese Selimovica; is that consistent with what you've just answered?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I can't remember where Mese Selimovica Bulevar is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: My understanding is that it's the main road along which the tram lines run. Did you walk along the road that the tram lines run along?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, up to Dolac Malta.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Along that same road, you would pass the Holiday Inn; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I think we better bring the map back up. If we can please again have Exhibit P30766.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps could we ask, you said you walked that road where the tram lines are up to Dolac Malta. What did you do at Dolac Malta? Did you leave that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In which direction, to the left or to the right when you were heading for Marin Dvor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is not indicated on the map as marked, it seems.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, can you give me one moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we're a little confused. If you look at the map on the screen in front of you, you drew a red line in the Milosevic trial and that red line continues along the road where the tram lines are and it continues along that road past the location that you've just mentioned, Dolac Malta. Is the map on the screen in front of you, does that represent the route that you walked to get to the Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: To Dolac Malta, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And your testimony now is that at Dolac Malta you turned --

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Left, because that's where the infirmary was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Can I ask you, in a pen that's blue, can you please draw starting at Dolac Malta --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, could we first ask the witness. You said: To the left, that's where the infirmary was. What infirmary are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the infirmary of the factory where I worked, because I had to get referrals to the hospital or any other doctor there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you first went to the infirmary and from there you went to Kosevo hospital. Is that ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you need a referral every time you went to Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, every time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you go there with such frequency, why would it be necessary to get a referral every single time you go to Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and would you then continue your road to the Kosevo hospital, again through Dolac Malta, on the main road where the tram tracks are or did you take a different route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I told you, I went about 200 metres to the left from Dolac Malta, to where my infirmary was. And then I went 500 metres more along the tram tracks, along the railway station, into the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. MacGregor, I leave it further in your hands. There may be other trams as well going in east-westerly direction, at least at some spots, I do not know. But I don't know how important the precise route is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'd like to ask a few more questions. I'm actually having trouble understanding the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If you could please, with the blue pen, starting at Dolac Malta, show the route from that location to Kosevo hospital.

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Could you enlarge this a bit because I can't see a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this large enough for you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I can see. Can I draw the line?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Is the pen working?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the pen is working, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, so you've marked Dolac Malta. Can you please continue to draw the line where you walked from that point?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes. It would go like this. I didn't do this very well, but that's the line. I would pass on this side up to Marin Dvor, the military hospital is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That is very helpful. It looks like you would for a -- for some distance you would -- okay. My comments aren't necessary. I understand the drawing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Can I ask that this be admitted as an exhibit with the drawings of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30766 as marked by the witness receives number P6576, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted under seal. Please proceed, Ms. MacGregor. And we have green light for an extended session of 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber urges you to --

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also to leave time for Mr. Ivetic for two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: In your statement at paragraph 13 and again today during your testimony, you discuss seeing two ABiH mortars on the grounds of the military hospital by Marin Dvor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, within the compound of the military hospital at Marin Dvor there were two artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: In this same paragraph, which is 13 of your statement, you describe: "On one occasion when I was walking towards the Kosevo hospital, I heard and saw the Muslims firing mortars at the Serbian positions." And to be clear, you're talking about something you saw at the military hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: And this paragraph describes the one time that you saw mortars on the military hospital ground being fired?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: It was not once, several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Was there something about this one occasion that caused you to describe it specifically in this statement?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Maybe some things were left unsaid, but I just wanted to say that from that location, from health institutions, artillery was firing at Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: We have evidence in our record from a doctor who worked at the military hospital starting in May 1992 and throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm referring to Witness Bakir Nakas.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Now, he testified that he stayed at the hospital practically day and night around-the-clock and that no unit fired anywhere in the vicinity of the hospital, nor did he receive any reports from security that any such firing happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I refer to transcript reference 8677.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: According to this witness, there was not a single military-related facility in the vicinity of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's at that witness's statement which is Exhibit P941.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'm asking you, can you really say with certainty that you saw two mortars on the hospital grounds at the state hospital?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Well, somebody probably ordered that witness what he's supposed to say. Nobody ordered me anything. I said that to the lawyers too. I'm just saying what I saw. And I'm claim that I saw that not only once but several times. Let me just add something else. From the health centre -- oh, oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we're trying to -- I'm doing my best to get done with your testimony today so please help me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If I can please have Exhibit 30 -- excuse me, transcript -- excuse me, 65 ter 30763, page 74 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, again I'm going to refer to an excerpt from your Milosevic testimony. During that trial, the Prosecutor asked you if you were aware that in your time in Sarajevo there was a considerable presence of United Nations monitors and personnel. And I'm going to read to you your answer. I'm starting at line 6 of the page in front of us. "I never saw them. I would probably seek help from them. I had heard of them being present there." You were then asked: "... you never saw United Nations personnel? "A. No. "Did you ever see United Nations APC or a United Nations vehicle ... "A. No." Mr. Witness, so we are clear, from May 1992 until the middle of 1996, you did not see UN personnel in the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I was interested in getting home alive because from every high-rise and from every window there were barrels, guns hanging. From Marin Dvor, I would walk by the hospital, I took this other route. If it weren't for the building of the Executive Council, who knows how many civilians they killed during the war, Croats, Muslims, and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: My question was: Did you ever see UN personnel in the city of Sarajevo during the war? That's a yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I don't know anything. No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: What about UN vehicles?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Can I please have Exhibit 30767 -- excuse me, 65 ter, and page 2 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'm going to be showing you a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Page 2, please. Oh, excuse me, that is page 2. You know what, can we please go to the first page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you recognise the Assembly building as the building on the right side of this picture?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Maybe. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Do you see the vehicle, the UN APC, in front of the building in that picture?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. I don't know whose vehicle it is, but I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Well, you may not be able to see, but the letters "UN" are written on the vehicle near the head of the man on the bicycle. There's also a --

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I see that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: There's also a blue flag, the UN flag, coming off the vehicle. Do you see on the left-hand side a container?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: When you walked along this street during the war, did you see this kind of vehicle along the road?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No -- well, I wasn't interested. I've already told you, I was interested in getting home alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Did you see that kind of container that's featured on the left side of the picture?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: Well, to this day there are so many containers like that in Sarajevo, in front of those private businesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If we can look at the second page of this exhibit again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: You'll see in this picture there's another picture of the containers. Are you aware these containers were used to protect civilians walking along this route?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: No. I did not see those containers anywhere along the route that I took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, were you at all aware that containers were used to protect pedestrians in the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe. But I've told you, on my way to the factory there weren't any containers anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And on your way to Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not there either. At least I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you from your testimony again in Milosevic. This is transcript reference 8858. You were being asked about walking down this route. "On your trip, sir, down this road that you took to the Kosevo hospital, did you ever notice barricades, containers, and other contraptions that were used to protection civilians?" Your answer: "I was only looking at the containers and barricades." Now, you've just said at line -- page 94, line 23, when asked a similar question: I did not see those containers anywhere along that route. And you said that you were not looking at anything, you were just trying to stay alive. Can you explain why in the Milosevic trial you testified that you did see such barricades?

utterances.speaker: GRM311
utterances.text: I doubt I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Can I please have this exhibit entered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30767 receives number P6577, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. If the parties are interested in verifying the audio from the Milosevic case, of course there's always an opportunity to do that. I'm looking at the clock, Ms. MacGregor, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I realise -- I'm not finished. The answers of the witness haven't been as I expected and I expect I would need an additional 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm still at two or three questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is inclined not to push any further and to -- and to continue tomorrow. But before doing so, I would like to move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber has considered the reasons why you would prefer to go home today. The Chamber has decided that we'll unfortunately have to go on tomorrow. It will not take much time tomorrow morning, most likely only half a session or even less, that means that most likely we'll conclude before 10.30. But we need your presence still tomorrow. And before you'll be escorted out of the courtroom, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether it is testimony you have given today or the testimony that is still there to be given tomorrow. And we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. I announce already to the public that once we are back in closed session, that we'll adjourn for the day and that we'll resume tomorrow, Friday, the 6th of June, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I. Yes, Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If I may raise one administrative matter. If I could have 65 ter 30766, which is the map before he marked in it zoomed out, if I could also ask that that be admitted as an exhibit because the map that we currently have in evidence doesn't show the entire map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the blue marking? I know that once we are zooming in and out that there are limitations of what can still be stored and not. Could you perhaps -- once we have adjourned check whether there's any technical problem. If not, a decision will be taken tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just to be clear, is that the map where the red line was drawn in the previous case?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That should be at least under seal, as you indicated earlier?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: You're correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You mean just the map as marked by the witness in the other case, without the blue markings? Or with the blue markings?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I actually would like there to be two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Because I think -- I'll talk with your staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then -- well, Madam Registrar is always of great assistance to us but is not our staff. Perhaps she would not even like to be our staff. We turn into closed session in order to adjourn for the day and for the witness to be allowed to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 6th day of June, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
